Class XElements

java.lang.Object
threepl.netlist.TDECode
threepl.netlist.GenFunctions
threepl.netlist.xilinx.XElements
All Implemented Interfaces:
TDEConstants, NetConstants, Constant
Direct Known Subclasses:
XFunctions
public abstract class XElements extends GenFunctions implements NetConstants, Constant, TDEConstants

This class contains methods which implement Xilinx common unified library elements. These are the low level elements from which the output EDIF netlist is generated. All higher level functions call these, directly or indirectly.

Elements specific to a particular FPGA family are contained in subclasses X2S, X3S, XCV, XC2V, XC2VP etc.

The arguments and return values are not a consistent scheme through all elements.

The arguments and return values are not a consistent scheme through all elements.

 The class structure is -

        TDECode           implementation of TDE modules - vendor independent
           |
      GenFunctions        general support methods - vendor independent
           |
       XElements          Xilinx general unified elements
           |
       XFunctions         Xilinx higher level functions
           |
       XTDECode           Xilinx implementation of TDE modules
           |
     ----------------------------
    /   /  |   \   \      \
 XC2S XCV XC3S XC2V XC2VP XC4V ......     Xilinx elements specific to FPGA families
All classes above starting with "X" are in subdirectory "xilinx".

All methods in the lowest subclasses override corresponding methods in class XElements which throw exceptions to pick up the use of special elements in FPGA families which do not have them.

TDE code generation methods are invoked using the FPGA family as the object instance.

    • selector

      public void selector(Net out, Net[] sel, Net[] data, int def)
      Construct a selector. This is not a basic element and must be converted to gates later. It is used as a go-between from a TDESELECT to gate elements. The TDESELECT cannot optimise duplicated data inputs as later TDECONNECT elements may later join nets that are not initially recognised as connected. Once the netlist has been built and is to be optimised these selector elements can have duplicate inputs removed as all nets will have been fully resolved. The select element can then be converted to basic gate form which may then be later optimised to family-specific elements (e.g. OR gates into a carry chain).
      Parameters:
      out - is the output net
      sel - is as array of select signals
      data - is as array of data signals
      def - is the default output if no selectors are true

    • MULT

      public void MULT(Net[] a, Net[] b, Net[] p, boolean asigned, boolean bsigned)
      A generic multiplier. This is replaced by one or more hardware multipliers in FPGAs that have multipliers or DSP blocks. In other cases this is replaced by a series of CLB adders. The replacement is performed in XNetlistOptimise.optimisegates().

      a - is the 1st input operand
      b - is the 2nd input operand
      p - is the product

      bsigned - is true if the 2nd operand is signed

    • ramallocate

      public void ramallocate(int awidth, int dwidth, Net wea, Net ena, Net rsta, Net clka, Net[] addra, Net[] dina, Net[] douta, Net web, Net enb, Net rstb, Net clkb, Net[] addrb, Net[] dinb, Net[] doutb, String[] init, String init0, String init1, ArrayList<String> properties)
      Partition block RAM memory into available elements and instantiate them. Multiple elements are used where the data width exceeds that available from one element. The depth is constrained by the maximum depth of an element. address and data width determine RAMB type. This method is overwritten in most FPGA family classes
      Parameters:
      awidth - address width requested
      dwidth - data width
      wea - port A write enable
      ena - port A enable
      rsta - port A reset
      clka - port A clock
      addra - port A address
      dina - port A data input
      douta - port A data output
      web - port B write enable
      enb - port B enable
      rstb - port B reset
      clkb - port B clock
      addrb - port B address
      dinb - port B data input
      doutb - port B data output
      init - initialisation array (binary strings) for requested address width.
      init0 - initial binary string value of output register port 0 (rmemory only)
      init1 - initial binary string value of output register port 1 (rmemory only)
      properties - properties (attributes such as writemode)

    • fifoallocate

      public void fifoallocate(int depth, int dwidth, Net push, Net pop, Net[] in, Net[] out, Net empty, Net full, Net[] rdcount, Net[] wrcount, Net reset, Net wclk, Net rclk)
      Partition a block RAM FIFO into available elements. Multiple elements are used where the data width exceeds that available from one element. The depth is constrained by the maximum depth of an element. address and data width determine FIFO type (18, 18_36, 36 or 36_72)
      Parameters:
      depth - depth requested
      dwidth - data width
      push - push input signal
      pop - pop input signal
      in - data input signal array
      out - data output signal signal array
      empty - empty output signal
      full - full output signal
      rdcount - port B enable
      wrcount - port B reset
      reset - reset input signal
      wclk - write clock
      rclk - read clock
